title: Pictures From Noise
objective: After this level you can explain how image generators learn to turn random noise, step by step, into a picture that matches a prompt.
summary: Diffusion models learn to remove noise added step by step to real images, then generate by denoising fresh random static, steered by a text prompt.

cards.headline: Many AI pictures start as static.
cards.body: Ask a diffusion image generator, the kind behind many popular tools, for a lighthouse at dusk and it doesn't sketch or paint. It starts from random noise and removes noise, step by step, until a lighthouse is left. The clever part is how it learned to clean.

cards.headline: Training: ruin pictures on purpose
cards.body: To train a diffusion model, real images are turned into pure noise by adding a little noise at each step. The model's job is to run the film backward. At each step it predicts the noise in the image and removes a fraction of it. Ruining pictures is easy; learning to undo the ruin is the whole skill.

cards.headline: Generating: from noise to lighthouse
cards.body: To make something new, a trained diffusion model starts from fresh random noise and removes noise step by step. A text prompt, interpreted by a separate language model, steers the result toward what you asked for. The influential 2020 paper by Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel at UC Berkeley used 1,000 steps.

cards.headline: Noise, in numbers
cards.body: Remember Level 5: each pixel's color is three numbers, red, green and blue, from 0 to 255. Add random noise to those numbers, step after step, and the picture ends up looking like TV static. Generating runs that the other way: the model changes the pixel numbers a little at each step until they form a picture.

cards.headline: Pictures from noise: developed
learned: Training adds noise to real images, step by step
The model learns to predict and remove that noise
Generating starts from random noise, steered by a prompt
Denoising changes pixel numbers until a picture appears

questions.prompt: What does a trained diffusion model start from when it makes a new image?

options.label: A stored photo that matches the prompt
options.rationale: It starts from noise, not from a saved picture.

options.label: A blank white canvas
options.rationale: It starts from random noise, not blank white.

options.label: A rough sketch drawn by a person
options.rationale: No sketch is needed; it removes noise step by step.

questions.explanation: Generation starts from random noise, which the model removes step by step.

questions.prompt: A friend says image generators just cut and paste pieces of stored photos. Which description fits how diffusion works?

options.label: It picks the stored photo closest to your prompt
options.rationale: Generation starts from random noise, not a stored photo.

options.label: It removes predicted noise step by step, steered by the prompt
It blends two random photos from the internet
options.rationale: No photos are blended; noise is removed step by step.

options.label: It paints strokes one by one like an artist
options.rationale: It changes the whole image a little at each step.

questions.explanation: The model learned to predict and remove noise; to generate, it denoises fresh random noise step by step, guided by the prompt.

questions.prompt: In Level 5, each pixel's color is three numbers from 0 to 255. What does a diffusion model change as it turns static into a picture?

options.label: Those pixel numbers, a little at each step
The number of pixels in the grid, adding more each step
options.rationale: The grid stays the same size; the values change.

options.label: The file's name and the date it was saved
options.rationale: Those don't change what the picture shows.

options.label: Only the single brightest pixel in the image
options.rationale: Every pixel's numbers change as noise is removed.

questions.explanation: Noise is random changes to pixel numbers; denoising adjusts those numbers step by step until they form an image.
